Rozsa et al. (2023) on DANDI:000341, part 2: RAF induction recordings¶

Paper: Rozsa, Toth, Olah, Baka, Lakovics, Barzo and Tamas (2023), Sci. Adv. 9, eade4511, doi:10.1126/sciadv.ade4511. Claims file: claims/rozsa-2023.yaml, written from the version of record (Europe PMC full text) and its supplement.

Dataset: DANDI:000341, version 0.241220.1312 (doi:10.48324/dandi.000341/0.241220.1312), the only published version; the paper cites the dandiset without a version.

This notebook covers the folders Human_persistent_RAF (313 files) and Rat_persistent_RAF (132 files), the RAF induction recordings. Each file is taken as one cell (checked for repeats below).

Revised after the first verification round: the threshold is found on a trace smoothed to the Methods' 10 kHz filter, artefact APs are removed before any analysis, RA-APs must have no positive current in absolute terms (holding current included), the mixture is fitted on robustly scaled features, and each result is also shown without the drug-treated files and without the cells that fire spontaneously before induction.

import zlib, time, resource, collections
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import raf

%matplotlib inline
pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 30)
PAPER = "rozsa-2023"


def seed(claim):
    return zlib.crc32(f"{PAPER}/{claim}".encode())


T0 = time.time()
assets = raf.list_assets()
groups = collections.defaultdict(list)
for a in assets:
    groups[a["path"].split("/")[0]].append(a)
res = {}
for g in ("Human_persistent_RAF", "Rat_persistent_RAF"):
    t = time.time()
    res[g] = raf.process_group(groups[g], workers=4)
    print(f"{g}: {len(res[g])} files, {sum(a['size'] for a in groups[g]) / 1e9:.0f} GB in "
          f"{(time.time() - t) / 60:.1f} min; peak memory "
          f"{resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss / 1e6:.1f} GB")

Human_persistent_RAF: 313 files, 147 GB in 16.0 min; peak memory 0.9 GB

Rat_persistent_RAF: 132 files, 113 GB in 11.4 min; peak memory 1.2 GB

Per-cell reduction¶

For each file: the induction sweeps (raf.induction_sweeps: shorter than 1 s, one positive step of 50 to 300 ms), AIS-APs (APs during positive current steps) and RA-APs by reading (c) of the claims file's header (raf.ra_aps_induction: APs after the first induction sweep with at most 5 pA of current at threshold, both relative to the holding level and in absolute terms, rebound APs within 0.3 s of a hyperpolarizing step left out). Artefact APs (threshold outside -80 to -10 mV or peak above 100 mV, raf.plausible) are removed first. cont marks the RA-APs of the continuous recording (sweeps without any step), which is what the Methods count ("number of RA-APs during continuous recording"). The baseline is the APs without current in the sweeps before the first induction sweep (raf.spontaneous_before). Sag from the sweeps with one hyperpolarizing step, taken before the first induction sweep where there are any.

def drugs_of(m):
    return sorted({v for k, v in m["pharmacology"].items() if "Name" in k and v != "NaN"})


cells = []
for g, sp in (("Human_persistent_RAF", "human"), ("Rat_persistent_RAF", "rat")):
    for p, (m, aps, sw, _) in res[g].items():
        n_main = int(aps.main.sum()) if len(aps) else 0
        aps = aps[aps.main & raf.plausible(aps)] if len(aps) else aps
        ais, ra, t0, runs = raf.ra_aps_induction(aps, sw)
        _, ra_rel, _, _ = raf.ra_aps_induction(aps, sw, absolute=False)
        stepless = set(sw[sw.nsteps == 0].series)
        ra = ra.assign(cont=ra.series.isin(stepless)) if len(ra) else ra.assign(cont=[])
        n_pre, n_pre_cont, pre_s = raf.spontaneous_before(aps, sw, t0)
        sag = sw.dropna(subset=["sag_a"]) if "sag_a" in sw else sw.iloc[:0]
        if len(sag) and np.isfinite(t0) and (sag.start < t0).any():
            sag = sag[sag.start < t0]
        v = sw[sw.chan.str.startswith("Vm")].sort_values("start")
        post = v[(v.start >= t0) & (v.nsteps == 0)] if np.isfinite(t0) else v.iloc[:0]
        cells.append(dict(species=sp, file=p.split("/")[-1], subject=m["subject_subject_id"], meta=m,
                          aps=aps, ais=ais, ra=ra, t0=t0, runs=runs, sag=sag,
                          n_main=n_main, n_art=n_main - len(aps), n_ra_rel=len(ra_rel),
                          n_pre=n_pre, n_pre_cont=n_pre_cont, pre_s=pre_s,
                          hold_post=float(post.hold.median()) if len(post) else np.nan,
                          hold_post_max=float(post.hold.max()) if len(post) else np.nan,
                          post_s=float((post.n / post.rate).sum()),
                          drugs=drugs_of(m), ca=m["pharmacology"].get("Ca (mM)", "NaN"),
                          mg=m["pharmacology"].get("Mg (mM)", "NaN"),
                          n_ind=len(raf.induction_sweeps(sw)), n_sweeps=len(v),
                          fingerprint=(len(v), tuple(v.vmed.round(3).head(20))),
                          rates=sorted(set(v.rate.round())), n_stim_pA=int(sw.get("stim_in_pA", pd.Series([False])).sum()),
                          n_stim_bad=int(sw.get("stim_bad", pd.Series([False])).sum()),
                          n_nostim_aps=int(aps.i_thr.isna().sum()) if len(aps) else 0))
for c in cells:
    c["clean"] = not c["drugs"]
    c["quiet_before"] = c["n_pre"] == 0
print(len(cells), "cells")

445 cells

C = pd.DataFrame([{k: v for k, v in c.items() if k in ("species", "file", "subject", "t0", "n_ind", "n_sweeps",
                                                       "n_stim_pA", "n_stim_bad", "n_main", "n_art", "n_nostim_aps",
                                                       "n_pre", "n_pre_cont", "pre_s", "hold_post", "hold_post_max",
                                                       "post_s", "clean", "ca", "mg")}
                  | {"n_ais": len(c["ais"]), "n_ra": len(c["ra"]), "n_ra_rel": c["n_ra_rel"], "n_sag": len(c["sag"])}
                  for c in cells])
for sp, d in C.groupby("species"):
    print(f"{sp}: files {len(d)}, subjects {d.subject.nunique()}, files with induction sweeps "
          f"{int((d.n_ind > 0).sum())}, with sag sweeps {int((d.n_sag > 0).sum())}; sweeps per file median "
          f"{d.n_sweeps.median():.0f}; stimulus stored in pA in {int((d.n_stim_pA > 0).sum())} files, "
          f"unusable in {int((d.n_stim_bad > 0).sum())}")
    print(f"   APs (peak > 0 mV) {d.n_main.sum()}, of which artefacts removed (threshold outside -80 to -10 mV "
          f"or peak above 100 mV) {d.n_art.sum()}; APs in sweeps without a stimulus series (never RA-APs or "
          f"AIS-APs) {d.n_nostim_aps.sum()}")
rates = collections.Counter(r for c in cells for r in c["rates"])
print("sampling rates present (files):", dict(rates))
allaps = pd.concat([c["aps"].assign(species=c["species"], cell=i) for i, c in enumerate(cells) if len(c["aps"])],
                   ignore_index=True)
print(f"APs kept: {len(allaps)}; threshold {allaps.thr.min():.1f} to {allaps.thr.max():.1f} mV, "
      f"peak {allaps.peak.min():.1f} to {allaps.peak.max():.1f} mV, slope {allaps.slope.min():.1f} to {allaps.slope.max():.1f} mV/ms")
fp = collections.defaultdict(list)
for c in cells:
    fp[c["fingerprint"]].append(c["file"])
print("files with identical sweep fingerprints (same sweep count and median Vm of 20 sweeps):",
      [v for v in fp.values() if len(v) > 1] or "none")
words = collections.Counter(d for c in cells for d in c["drugs"])
print("drugs named in general/pharmacology (files):", dict(words))
print("files with any drug named:", dict(C.assign(drug=~C.clean).groupby("species").drug.sum()))
print("Ca and Mg of the bath (mM), files:", dict(collections.Counter((c["species"], c["ca"], c["mg"]) for c in cells)))
kcl = [c["file"] for c in cells if any(("kcl" in str(v).lower() or "potassium" in str(v).lower() or "k+" in str(v).lower())
                                       for v in list(c["meta"]["pharmacology"].values()) + [c["meta"].get("session_description"), c["meta"].get("experiment_description")])]
print("files whose metadata mention KCl or potassium:", kcl or "none")
ctype = [c["file"] for c in cells if any(k.lower().startswith(("celltype", "anatomy")) for k in c["meta"]["pharmacology"])]
print("files with a cell class field:", len(ctype))
print("session descriptions:", dict(collections.Counter(c["meta"]["session_description"] for c in cells)))
print("subject descriptions:", dict(collections.Counter(str(c["meta"].get("subject_description")) for c in cells).most_common(8)))
# Session identifiers that also occur in the active-slice folders (the same cell deposited twice?).
import re
ses = lambda p: re.search(r"ses-([^_]+)_icephys", p).group(1)
active = {ses(a["path"]) for g in ("In_vitro_oscillation_Rat", "In_vitro_Human_elevated_neuronal_activity") for a in groups[g]}
shared = [c for c in cells if ses(c["file"]) in active]
for c in cells:
    c["in_active_folder"] = ses(c["file"]) in active
print(f"induction files whose session identifier also names an active-slice file: {len(shared)} "
      f"({sum(c['species'] == 'human' for c in shared)} human, {sum(c['species'] == 'rat' for c in shared)} rat); "
      f"with a drug named: {sum(not c['clean'] for c in shared)}")
size = collections.defaultdict(list)
for a in groups["Human_persistent_RAF"] + groups["Rat_persistent_RAF"]:
    size[a["size"]].append(a["path"].split("/")[-1])
same = [v for v in size.values() if len(v) > 1]
fpd = {c["file"]: c["fingerprint"] for c in cells}
print("induction files of identical size:", same or "none",
      "; identical fingerprints among them:", [v for v in same if len({fpd.get(f) for f in v}) == 1] or "none")

Holding current and spontaneous firing before induction (verifier, round 1). hold_post is the median holding current of the stepless sweeps after the first induction sweep, hold_post_max its maximum; n_pre the APs without current before the first induction sweep (n_pre_cont of them in stepless sweeps), over pre_s seconds of stepless recording. n_ra_rel is the RA-AP count when the current is taken relative to the holding level only (the rule of the first round), n_ra with the absolute current also at most 5 pA.

Threshold detection on a synthetic AP (a 1 mV/ms ramp, then an exponential upstroke whose dV/dt crosses 5 mV/ms at a known time, Gaussian noise of 0.2 mV), at the sampling rates in the files.

In [5]:
def synthetic(rate, noise, rng):
    t = np.arange(0, 0.05, 1 / rate)
    v = np.full_like(t, -65.0)
    r_ = (t > 0.02) & (t <= 0.03)
    v[r_] += (t[r_] - 0.02) * 1000
    v[t > 0.03] = -55.0
    k = (t > 0.03) & (t < 0.033)
    v[k] = np.minimum(-55 + np.cumsum(np.exp((t[k] - 0.03) * 1000 / 0.25)) / (rate / 1000), 30)
    v[t >= 0.033] = -60.0
    return v + rng.normal(0, noise, len(v)), 0.03 + 0.25e-3 * np.log(5)


rng = np.random.default_rng(seed("fig1c-ra-lower-threshold-slope"))
for rate in (5000, 16667, 25000, 50000, 100000, 200000):
    out = [raf._ap_table(synthetic(rate, 0.2, rng)[0], rate, None) for _ in range(30)]
    th = [o[0]["thr"] for o in out if o]
    sl = [o[0]["slope"] for o in out if o]
    print(f"{rate:6d} Hz: detected {len(th)}/30, threshold median {np.median(th):.2f} mV (true about -53.7), "
          f"slope median {np.median(sl):.2f} mV/ms")

Reading (b): one mixture per species on all its kept APs, fitted to a seeded draw of 200,000 of them (raf.gmm_classes). The component means, SDs and weights are printed, with whether the RA component (lower threshold) also has the lower slope, as the paper describes RA-APs.

allaps["gmm_ra"] = False
GMM = {}
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4))
for ax, sp in zip(axs, ("human", "rat")):
    idx = (allaps.species == sp).to_numpy()
    sd_ = seed("fig1ab-raf-patterns") + (0 if sp == "human" else 1)
    lab, info = raf.gmm_classes(allaps[idx], sd_)
    allaps.loc[idx, "gmm_ra"] = lab
    GMM[sp] = info
    print(sp, {k: (round(v, 3) if isinstance(v, float) else v) for k, v in info.items()})

In [7]:
SUBSETS = {"all": lambda c: True, "drug-free": lambda c: c["clean"],
           "quiet before induction": lambda c: c["quiet_before"]}


def cell_epochs(c, reading, which):
    """RAF epochs of a cell. which: 'cont' (continuous recording, reading (c)), 'all' (with the
    interstimulus intervals, reading (c)), 'gmm' (continuous recording, RA-APs that the mixture
    also labels RA, reading (b)). reading: 'i' one epoch per cell, 'ii' one per induction run."""
    ra = c["ra"]
    if not len(ra):
        return []
    if which == "cont":
        ra = ra[ra.cont]
    elif which == "gmm":
        ra = ra[ra.cont & ra.gmm]
    return raf.epochs(ra.t_abs, None if reading == "i" else c["runs"])


def summarize(sp, reading, which, subset="all"):
    E = pd.DataFrame([e | {"file": c["file"]} for c in cells if c["species"] == sp and SUBSETS[subset](c)
                      for e in cell_epochs(c, reading, which)])
    if not len(E):
        return E, {}
    E["persistent"] = E.freq > 5
    P, S = E[E.persistent], E[~E.persistent]
    out = dict(n_epochs=len(E), n_persistent=len(P), n_sporadic=len(S),
               pers_n_median=P.n.median(), pers_freq_median=P.freq.median(), pers_dur_median=P.duration.median(),
               pers_dur_mean=P.duration.mean(), pers_dur_min=P.duration.min(), pers_dur_max=P.duration.max(),
               spor_n_median=S.n.median(), spor_freq_median=S.freq.median(),
               all_dur_median=E.duration.median(), all_dur_mean=E.duration.mean(),
               all_dur_min=E.duration.min(), all_dur_max=E.duration.max(),
               pers_n_sd=P.n.std(), pers_freq_sd=P.freq.std(), spor_n_sd=S.n.std(), spor_freq_sd=S.freq.std())
    return E, out


def judge(out, exp, keys):
    hits = []
    for k, (v, tol) in zip(keys, exp):
        x = out.get(k, np.nan)
        hits.append(bool(np.isfinite(x) and abs(x - v) <= tol))
    return hits

fig1ab-raf-patterns¶

Human layer 1 interneurons show two forms of retroaxonal firing (RAF) after induction, persistent RAF with barrages of RA-APs at high frequency (median 88 RA-APs, 13.9 Hz; duration median 17.1 s, mean 68.4 s, from 0.18 to 2809 s) and sporadic RAF with a few RA-APs at low frequency (median 8 RA-APs, 0.31 Hz).

Readings: epochs (i) one per cell, (ii) one per induction run; RA-APs of the continuous recording by reading (c), with the interstimulus intervals included as a variant, and those the mixture also labels RA by reading (b). The durations are judged under persistent RAF and shown over all epochs. Each reading on all cells, on the drug-free files, and on the cells without spontaneous APs before induction.

Result: not reproduced. Persistent and sporadic epochs both occur under every reading on all cells, but at most two of the eight values are within tolerance under any reading or subset (the cells quiet before induction, RA-APs with the interstimulus intervals, one epoch per run: maximum duration 2616 s and sporadic frequency 0.294 Hz). The first reading (continuous recording, one epoch per cell, all cells) has none. The mixture of reading (b) fails its check (its RA component has the steeper mean slope, about 6.9 against 1.9 mV/ms in human, and its size changes with the seed from about 88,000 to about 2,450,000 APs), so the gmm rows are not a reading of the paper's classes.

fig1c-ra-lower-threshold-slope¶

RA-APs have a lower somatic threshold potential and a lower pre-AP depolarization slope than AIS-APs, during persistent and during sporadic RAF.

Reading (c): AIS-APs during the current pulses, RA-APs after induction (interstimulus intervals and continuous recording), within the cells whose one epoch (reading (i), RA-APs of the continuous recording) is persistent or sporadic. APs pooled; the paper's rule (KS normality, then t test or Mann-Whitney U). Per-cell medians as a variant. Then the same comparison within each sampling rate, since the rates differ between the protocols.

SEL = {}
for sp in ("human", "rat"):
    for pattern in ("persistent", "sporadic"):
        A, B, PA, PB = [], [], [], []
        for c in cells:
            if c["species"] != sp:
                continue
            ep = cell_epochs(c, "i", "cont")
            if not ep:
                continue
            pers = ep[0]["freq"] > 5
            if pers != (pattern == "persistent"):
                continue
            A.append(c["ais"]); B.append(c["ra"])
            PA.append(c["ais"][["thr", "slope"]].median()); PB.append(c["ra"][["thr", "slope"]].median())
        if not A:
            print(sp, pattern, "no cells"); continue
        A, B = pd.concat(A), pd.concat(B)
        SEL[(sp, pattern)] = (A, B)
        PA, PB = pd.DataFrame(PA), pd.DataFrame(PB)
        for q in ("thr", "slope"):
            t, p = raf.paper_test(B[q], A[q])
            tc = stats.mannwhitneyu(PB[q].dropna(), PA[q].dropna()).pvalue if len(PB[q].dropna()) and len(PA[q].dropna()) else np.nan
            print(f"{sp:5s} {pattern:10s} {q:5s}: cells {len(PA)}; AIS-AP median {A[q].median():7.2f} (n={len(A)}), "
                  f"RA-AP median {B[q].median():7.2f} (n={len(B)}); {t} P = {p:.2g}; per-cell medians "
                  f"{PA[q].median():.2f} vs {PB[q].median():.2f}, Mann-Whitney P = {tc:.2g}; "
                  f"cells with RA-AP median below AIS-AP median {int((PB[q] < PA[q]).sum())} of {int((PB[q].notna() & PA[q].notna()).sum())}")
print()
print("By sampling rate (human and rat, both patterns pooled): median threshold (mV) and slope (mV/ms)")
for sp in ("human", "rat"):
    A = pd.concat([SEL[k][0] for k in SEL if k[0] == sp]).assign(cls="AIS")
    B = pd.concat([SEL[k][1] for k in SEL if k[0] == sp]).assign(cls="RA")
    D = pd.concat([A, B])
    D["rate_khz"] = (D.rate / 1000).round(1)
    t = D.groupby(["rate_khz", "cls"]).agg(n=("thr", "size"), thr=("thr", "median"), slope=("slope", "median")).unstack("cls")
    print(sp)
    print(t.round(2).to_string())

Result: reproduced. In the 24 human persistent cells RA-APs have a lower threshold (median -59.6 against -44.1 mV) and slope (0.77 against 1.79 mV/ms), and in the 119 sporadic cells too (-61.4 against -44.8 mV, 0.74 against 2.18 mV/ms), with Mann-Whitney P printed as 0 (below double precision) and per-cell P from 1.4e-16 to 0.0006. The order holds within each human sampling rate that has both classes (10 to 100 kHz).

fig1d-human-raf-proportion and figs1b-rat-raf-proportion¶

About one-fourth of tested human layer 1 interneurons (87 of 385) show RAF. About a third of tested rat layer 1 interneurons (102 of 259) show RAF.

A cell shows RAF when at least one RA-AP occurs after induction. Tested cells are the files with induction sweeps; all files are shown as the other denominator. RA-APs by reading (c) (with or without the interstimulus intervals) and by reading (b) (reading (c) RA-APs the mixture also labels RA). At least two RA-APs is shown as a variant against single spurious events. Subsets: all tested cells; drug-free files; cells with spontaneous APs before induction counted as without RAF, or left out.

Result (fig1d-human-raf-proportion): not reproduced. With at least one RA-AP, as the criterion says, 301 of 307 human cells (0.980) have RAF by reading (c) and 159 (0.518) on the continuous recording alone; the drug-free files give 0.976 and 0.446, and counting the cells that fire before induction as without RAF gives 0.586 and 0.280. Only variants outside the criterion fall within tolerance: at least two continuous-recording RA-APs with the cells firing before induction counted as without RAF (0.241), and a reading (b) row whose mixture fails its check (0.238).

Result (figs1b-rat-raf-proportion): not reproduced. 115 of 118 rat cells (0.975) have RA-APs by reading (c) and 97 (0.822) on the continuous recording; the lowest fraction in the table is 0.500, against 0.394.

fig2e-sag-species and fig2e-sag-raf-smaller¶

Human layer 1 interneurons have a higher somatic sag fraction than rat ones (0.15 against 0.04). In both species, interneurons with RAF have smaller somatic sag fractions than those without (human 0.11 against 0.16; rat 0.02 against 0.06).

Per cell, the sag of one step sweep: the most hyperpolarizing step, or the step whose peak is nearest -90 mV; formula (a) or (b) (raf._sag). RAF status (at least one RA-AP) by each reading of fig1d: reading (c) with the interstimulus intervals, reading (c) on the continuous recording only, and reading (b); over the tested cells with sag sweeps (the denominator of fig1d) and the drug-free ones among them. All files with sag sweeps, untested ones counted as without RAF, are shown for comparison.

Result: partially reproduced, resting on the RAF reading. On the tested cells, with RAF status from the RA-APs of the continuous recording (reading (c) without the interstimulus intervals), rat cells with RAF have the lower sag at P < 0.001 (formula (a), most hyperpolarizing step: 0.060, n = 95, against 0.125, n = 20, Mann-Whitney P = 0.00039), while human cells do not (0.186 against 0.211, P = 0.12). The rat result is fragile: the step nearest -90 mV gives P = 0.0080 and the drug-free files P = 0.0061. Counting the files without induction sweeps as without RAF, as the round-2 version did, gives rat P = 2.8e-05. With the interstimulus intervals neither species reaches P < 0.001 (rat 3 cells without RAF, P = 0.036; human 6, P = 0.54). No reading has more than one of the four medians within tolerance. Reading (b) gives the human difference at P < 0.001, but its mixture fails its check. The continuous-recording reading is the assumption: the Methods count RA-APs "during continuous recording" and start that recording once APs appear in the interstimulus interval (Methods, "Analysis of RAF patterns" and "Induction protocol of RAF").

Summary¶

Claim Outcome
fig1ab-raf-patterns not reproduced
fig1c-ra-lower-threshold-slope reproduced
fig1d-human-raf-proportion not reproduced
fig1f-human-raf-ngfc blocked, metadata_insufficient
figs1b-rat-raf-proportion not reproduced
figs1d-rat-raf-values not reproduced
fig1g-rat-raf-ngfc blocked, metadata_insufficient
fig2e-sag-species partially reproduced
fig2e-sag-raf-smaller partially reproduced (assumed)
fig2il-kcl-induces-ra-aps blocked, data_missing

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. Induction sweeps, AIS-APs and RA-APs are rebuilt from the stimulus and the traces (reading (c) of the claims file), as the files carry no labels; epochs are one per cell or one per induction run, as the claims file names. Sag is taken on the step sweeps before induction with a formula the paper does not give (two readings). Each result is also shown on the drug-free files and on the cells that do not fire before induction. The two-component mixture of reading (b) does not recover the paper's classes in these recordings (its lower-threshold component has the steeper slope, and its size depends on the seed), so no outcome rests on it.

What was found about the dataset. The folders hold 313 human and 132 rat files against 385 and 259 tested cells, and nearly every cell in them fires APs without current after induction, so they appear to be a selection the dandiset does not describe. 124 human and 33 rat cells fire spontaneous APs before induction. 58 human and 94 rat files list drugs or a changed calcium concentration. No file names a cell class or a KCl application. Sampling rates range from 5 to 200 kHz.
